newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Rwandan minister says aid corridors not feasible.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan minister says aid corridors not feasible.

text.p: Rwandan Foreign Minister Anastase Gasana said on Monday he did not think it was feasible to set up "humanitarian corridors" to allow Rwandan refugees caught up in fighting in eastern Zaire to return home.
"No we don't believe in it," he told Belgian BRTN television when asked the question.

Gasana, in Brussels for talks with his Belgian counterpart Erik Derycke and Secretary of State for Cooperation and Development Reginald Moreels, said the Belgian government should put pressure on Zaire to enter dialogue with Rwanda.

Moreels said earlier in the day that Belgium would discuss with Rwanda setting up protected humanitarian corridors to help refugees in Zaire threatened by the cross-border fighting return to Rwanda or Burundi.
"Secondly we will repeat the government's clear warning to Rwanda (not) to enter Zairean territory," Moreels said. Belgium has also warned Zaire against "provocation" in the conflict.
Moreels and Derycke were scheduled to give a news conference later on Monday, and Gasana was due to hold a news conference in Brussels on Tuesday.
Fighting between Tutsi rebels and the Zairean army in eastern Zaire forced the evacuation on Saturday of the last foreign aid workers and left refugees without U.N. protectors.
Belgium is the former colonial power of the sprawling central African country, while its smaller neighbours Rwanda and Burundi were once Belgian protectorates.

It has ruled out sending any troops to the region but Moreels said the government would examine how to support logistically and financially any African military force set up to protect such humanitarian corridors.

When Rwanda exploded into violence in 1994, 10 Belgian paratroopers were slaughtered by extremist Hutu militiamen at the start of a genocide in which about one million people, mainly Tutsis, were killed.
Stepping up Belgium's diplomatic efforts, Derycke said on Saturday he was sending a high-level mission to the Zairean capital Kinshasa.
